You will get suggestions and help as you start.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:CreateAccount?campaign=wtg-enUS-2025)  [More ways to give](https://wikimediafoundation.org/give/#ways-to-give)  Fractal related to the mandelbrot set

A **Douady rabbit** is a [fractal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fractal) derived from the [Julia set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filled_Julia_set) of the function      f  c   ( z ) =  z  2   + c   {\textstyle f_{c}(z)=z^{2}+c}  , when [parameter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parameter_(computer_programming))     c   {\displaystyle c}   is near the center of one of the [period three bulbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set#Main_cardioid_and_period_bulbs) of the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set) for a [complex quadratic map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_quadratic_map).

It is named after [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France) [mathematician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematician) [Adrien Douady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrien_Douady).

 [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Douady_rabbit%2C_plotted_with_Matplotlb.svg/330px-Douady_rabbit%2C_plotted_with_Matplotlb.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Douady_rabbit,_plotted_with_Matplotlb.svg)An example of a Douady rabbit. The colors show the number of iterations required to [escape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plotting_algorithms_for_the_Mandelbrot_set#Escape_time_algorithm).

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=1)]

The Douady rabbit is generated by iterating the [Mandelbrot set map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set)      z  n + 1   =  z  n   2   + c   {\displaystyle z_{n+1}=z_{n}^{2}+c}   on the [complex plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_plane), where parameter     c   {\displaystyle c}   is fixed to lie in one of the two period three bulb off the main [cardioid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardioid) and     z   {\displaystyle z}   ranging over the plane. The resulting image can be colored by corresponding each pixel with a starting value      z  0     {\displaystyle z_{0}}   and calculating the amount of [iterations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iteration) required before the value of      z  n     {\displaystyle z_{n}}   escapes a bounded region, after which it will diverge toward [infinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinity).

It can also be described using the *[logistic map form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_quadratic_polynomial#Forms)* of the [complex quadratic map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_quadratic_map), specifically

      z  n + 1   =   M    z  n   := γ  z  n    (  1 −  z  n    )  .   {\displaystyle z_{n+1}={\mathcal {M}}z_{n}:=\gamma z_{n}\left(1-z_{n}\right).}

which is equivalent to

w  n + 1   =  w  n   2   + c   {\displaystyle w_{n+1}=w_{n}^{2}+c}  .

Irrespective of the specific iteration used, the [filled Julia set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filled_Julia_set) associated with a given value of     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   (or     μ   {\displaystyle \mu }  ) consists of all starting points      z  0     {\displaystyle z_{0}}   (or      w  0     {\displaystyle w_{0}}  ) for which the iteration remains bounded. Then, the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set) consists of those values of     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   (or     μ   {\displaystyle \mu }  ) for which the associated filled Julia set is connected. The Mandelbrot set can be viewed with respect to either     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   or     μ   {\displaystyle \mu }  .

 [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/MandelbrotLambda.jpg/500px-MandelbrotLambda.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MandelbrotLambda.jpg)The Mandelbrot set in the     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   plane[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/MandelbrotMuDouadyRabbit.jpg/250px-MandelbrotMuDouadyRabbit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MandelbrotMuDouadyRabbit.jpg)The Mandelbrot set in the     μ   {\displaystyle \mu }   plane

Noting that     μ   {\displaystyle \mu }   is invariant under the substitution     γ → 2 − γ   {\displaystyle \gamma \to 2-\gamma }  , the Mandelbrot set with respect to     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   has additional horizontal symmetry. Since     z   {\displaystyle z}   and     w   {\displaystyle w}   are [affine transformations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affine_transformation) of one another, or more specifically a similarity transformation, consisting of only scaling, rotation and translation, the filled Julia sets look [similar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Similarity_(geometry)) for either form of the iteration given above.

## Detailed description

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=2)] [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/DouadyRabbitInExponentialFamily.jpg/250px-DouadyRabbitInExponentialFamily.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DouadyRabbitInExponentialFamily.jpg)Douady rabbit in an exponential family [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Rabbit-lamination.png/250px-Rabbit-lamination.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rabbit-lamination.png)[Lamination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamination_(topology)) of the rabbit Julia set [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Douday_rabbit_rough_dynamics.png/250px-Douday_rabbit_rough_dynamics.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Douday_rabbit_rough_dynamics.png)Representation of the dynamics inside the rabbit

You can also describe the Douady rabbit utilising the Mandelbrot set with respect to     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   as shown in the graph above. In this figure, the Mandelbrot set superficially appears as two back-to-back [unit disks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_disk) with *sprouts* or *buds*, such as the sprouts at the one- and five-o'clock positions on the right disk or the sprouts at the seven- and eleven-o'clock positions on the left disk. When     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   is within one of these four sprouts, the associated filled Julia set in the mapping plane is said to be a Douady rabbit. For these values of     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }  , it can be shown that       M     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}}   has     z = 0   {\displaystyle z=0}   and one other point as unstable (repelling) fixed points, and     z = ∞   {\displaystyle z=\infty }   as an attracting fixed point. Moreover, the map        M    3     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}^{3}}   has three attracting fixed points. A Douady rabbit consists of the three attracting fixed points      z  1     {\displaystyle z_{1}}  ,      z  2     {\displaystyle z_{2}}  , and      z  3     {\displaystyle z_{3}}   and their basins of attraction.

For example, Figure 4 shows the Douady rabbit in the     z   {\displaystyle z}   plane when     γ =  γ  D   = 2.55268 − 0.959456 i   {\displaystyle \gamma =\gamma _{D}=2.55268-0.959456i}  , a point in the five-o'clock sprout of the right disk. For this value of     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }  , the map       M     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}}   has the repelling fixed points     z = 0   {\displaystyle z=0}   and     z = .656747 − .129015 i   {\displaystyle z=.656747-.129015i}  . The three attracting fixed points of        M    3     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}^{3}}   (also called period-three fixed points) have the locations

          z  1      = 0.499997032420304 − ( 1.221880225696050 ×  10  − 6   ) i         ( r e d )   ,      z  2      = 0.638169999974373 − ( 0.239864000011495 ) i         ( g r e e n )   ,      z  3      = 0.799901291393262 − ( 0.107547238170383 ) i         ( y e l l o w )   .       {\displaystyle {\begin{aligned}z_{1}&=0.499997032420304-(1.221880225696050\times 10^{-6})i{\;}{\;}{\mathrm {(red)} },\\z_{2}&=0.638169999974373-(0.239864000011495)i{\;}{\;}{\mathrm {(green)} },\\z_{3}&=0.799901291393262-(0.107547238170383)i{\;}{\;}{\mathrm {(yellow)} }.\end{aligned}}}

The red, green, and yellow points lie in the basins     B (  z  1   )   {\displaystyle B(z_{1})}  ,     B (  z  2   )   {\displaystyle B(z_{2})}  , and     B (  z  3   )   {\displaystyle B(z_{3})}   of        M    3     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}^{3}}  , respectively. The white points lie in the basin     B ( ∞ )   {\displaystyle B(\infty )}   of       M     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}}  .

The action of       M     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}}   on these fixed points is given by the relations       M    z  1   =  z  2     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}z_{1}=z_{2}}  ,       M    z  2   =  z  3     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}z_{2}=z_{3}}  , and       M    z  3   =  z  1     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}z_{3}=z_{1}}  .

Corresponding to these relations there are the results

           M   B (  z  1   )    = B (  z  2   )      o r        M        r e d   ⊆   g r e e n   ,       M   B (  z  2   )    = B (  z  3   )      o r        M        g r e e n   ⊆   y e l l o w   ,       M   B (  z  3   )    = B (  z  1   )      o r        M        y e l l o w   ⊆   r e d   .       {\displaystyle {\begin{aligned}{\mathcal {M}}B(z_{1})&=B(z_{2}){\;}{\mathrm {or} }{\;}{\mathcal {M}}{\;}{\mathrm {red} }\subseteq {\mathrm {green} },\\{\mathcal {M}}B(z_{2})&=B(z_{3}){\;}{\mathrm {or} }{\;}{\mathcal {M}}{\;}{\mathrm {green} }\subseteq {\mathrm {yellow} },\\{\mathcal {M}}B(z_{3})&=B(z_{1}){\;}{\mathrm {or} }{\;}{\mathcal {M}}{\;}{\mathrm {yellow} }\subseteq {\mathrm {red} }.\end{aligned}}}   [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/ColorDouadyRabbit1.jpg/500px-ColorDouadyRabbit1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ColorDouadyRabbit1.jpg)Figure 4: Douady rabbit for     γ = 2.55268 − 0.959456 i   {\displaystyle \gamma =2.55268-0.959456i}   or     μ = 0.122565 − 0.744864 i   {\displaystyle \mu =0.122565-0.744864i}

As a second example, Figure 5 shows a Douady rabbit when     γ = 2 −  γ  D   = − .55268 + .959456 i   {\displaystyle \gamma =2-\gamma _{D}=-.55268+.959456i}  , a point in the eleven-o'clock sprout on the left disk (    μ   {\displaystyle \mu }   is invariant under this transformation). This rabbit is more symmetrical in the plane. The period-three fixed points then are located at

          z  1      = 0.500003730675024 + ( 6.968273875812428 ×  10  − 6   ) i       (   r e d   ) ,      z  2      = − 0.138169999969259 + ( 0.239864000061970 ) i       (   g r e e n   ) ,      z  3      = − 0.238618870661709 − ( 0.264884797354373 ) i       (   y e l l o w   ) .       {\displaystyle {\begin{aligned}z_{1}&=0.500003730675024+(6.968273875812428\times 10^{-6})i{\;}{\;}({\mathrm {red} }),\\z_{2}&=-0.138169999969259+(0.239864000061970)i{\;}{\;}({\mathrm {green} }),\\z_{3}&=-0.238618870661709-(0.264884797354373)i{\;}{\;}({\mathrm {yellow} }).\end{aligned}}}

The repelling fixed points of       M     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}}   itself are located at     z = 0   {\displaystyle z=0}   and     z = 1.450795 + 0.7825835 i   {\displaystyle z=1.450795+0.7825835i}  . The three major lobes on the left, which contain the period-three fixed points      z  1     {\displaystyle z_{1}}  ,     z  2     {\displaystyle z_{2}}  , and      z  3     {\displaystyle z_{3}}  , meet at the fixed point     z = 0   {\displaystyle z=0}  , and their counterparts on the right meet at the point     z = 1   {\displaystyle z=1}  . It can be shown that the effect of       M     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}}   on points near the origin consists of a counterclockwise rotation about the origin of     arg ⁡ ( γ )   {\displaystyle \arg(\gamma )}  , or very nearly      120  ∘     {\displaystyle 120^{\circ }}  , followed by scaling (dilation) by a factor of      |  γ  |  = 1.1072538   {\displaystyle |\gamma |=1.1072538}  .

 [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/ColorDouadyRabbit2.jpg/500px-ColorDouadyRabbit2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ColorDouadyRabbit2.jpg)Figure 5: Douady rabbit for     γ = − 0.55268 + 0.959456 i   {\displaystyle \gamma =-0.55268+0.959456i}   or     μ = 0.122565 − 0.744864 i   {\displaystyle \mu =0.122565-0.744864i}

## Variants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=3)]

A *twisted rabbit*[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-1) is the composition of a rabbit [polynomial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynomial) with     n   {\displaystyle n}   powers of [Dehn twists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehn_twist) about its ears.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-2)

The *corabbit* is the symmetrical image of the rabbit. Here parameter     c ≈ − 0.1226 − 0.7449 i   {\displaystyle c\approx -0.1226-0.7449i}  . It is one of 2 other [polynomials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynomial) inducing the same [permutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permutation) of their post-critical set are the rabbit.

### 3D

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=4)]

The Julia set has no direct analog in three dimensions.

### 4D

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=5)]

A [quaternion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternion) Julia set with parameters     c = − 0.123 + 0.745 i   {\displaystyle c=-0.123+0.745i}   and a [cross-section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_section_(geometry)) in the     x y   {\displaystyle xy}   plane. The Douady rabbit is visible in the cross-section.

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Quaternion_Julia_Douady_rabbit.jpg/500px-Quaternion_Julia_Douady_rabbit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Quaternion_Julia_Douady_rabbit.jpg)

### Embedded

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Parabolic_julia_set_c_%3D_-1.125_%2B_0.21650635094611%2Ai.png/500px-Parabolic_julia_set_c_%3D_-1.125_%2B_0.21650635094611%2Ai.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Parabolic_julia_set_c_=_-1.125_+_0.21650635094611*i.png)

A small embedded [homeomorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeomorphic) copy of rabbit in the center of a Julia set[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-3)

### Fat

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=7)]

The *fat rabbit* or *chubby rabbit* has c at the root of the 1/3-[limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set#Geometry) of the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set). It has a [parabolic fixed point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodic_points_of_complex_quadratic_mappings) with 3 [petals](https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Fractals/Iterations%20in%20the%20complex%20plane/parabolic).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-4)

- [![Fat rabbit](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/Parabolic_Julia_set_for_internal_angle_1_over_3.png/120px-Parabolic_Julia_set_for_internal_angle_1_over_3.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Parabolic_Julia_set_for_internal_angle_1_over_3.png)Fat rabbit
- [![Parabolic chessboard](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Parabolic_chessboard_for_internal_angle_1_over_3.png/120px-Parabolic_chessboard_for_internal_angle_1_over_3.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Parabolic_chessboard_for_internal_angle_1_over_3.png)Parabolic chessboard

### n-th eared

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=8)]

In general, the rabbit for the     p e r i o d − ( n + 1 )   {\displaystyle period-(n+1)}  th bulb of the main cardioid will have     n   {\displaystyle n}   ears[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-5) For example, a period four bulb rabbit has three ears.

## Twisted rabbit problem

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=10)]

In the early 1980s, Hubbard posed the so-called twisted rabbit problem, a polynomial classification problem. The goal is to determine Thurston equivalence types[*[definition needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please_clarify)*] of functions of [complex numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_number) that usually are not given by a formula (these are called topological polynomials):[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-7)

- given a [topological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topology) quadratic whose branch point is periodic with period three, determining which quadratic polynomial it is Thurston equivalent to
- determining the [equivalence class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equivalence_class) of twisted rabbits, i.e. composite of the rabbit polynomial with nth powers of Dehn twists about its ears.

The problem was originally solved by [Laurent Bartholdi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurent_Bartholdi) and Volodymyr Nekrashevych[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-8) using iterated [monodromic groups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monodromic_group). The generalization of the problem to the case where the number of post-critical points is arbitrarily large has been solved as well.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-9)

A **Douady rabbit** is a [fractal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fractal) derived from the [Julia set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filled_Julia_set) of the function      f  c   ( z ) =  z  2   + c   {\textstyle f_{c}(z)=z^{2}+c}  , when [parameter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parameter_(computer_programming))     c   {\displaystyle c}   is near the center of one of the [period three bulbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set#Main_cardioid_and_period_bulbs) of the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set) for a [complex quadratic map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_quadratic_map).

It is named after [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France) [mathematician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematician) [Adrien Douady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrien_Douady).

 [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Douady_rabbit%2C_plotted_with_Matplotlb.svg/330px-Douady_rabbit%2C_plotted_with_Matplotlb.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Douady_rabbit,_plotted_with_Matplotlb.svg)An example of a Douady rabbit. The colors show the number of iterations required to [escape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plotting_algorithms_for_the_Mandelbrot_set#Escape_time_algorithm).

Background

# Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=1)]

The Douady rabbit is generated by iterating the [Mandelbrot set map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set)      z  n + 1   =  z  n   2   + c   {\displaystyle z_{n+1}=z_{n}^{2}+c}   on the [complex plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_plane), where parameter     c   {\displaystyle c}   is fixed to lie in one of the two period three bulb off the main [cardioid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardioid) and     z   {\displaystyle z}   ranging over the plane. The resulting image can be colored by corresponding each pixel with a starting value      z  0     {\displaystyle z_{0}}   and calculating the amount of [iterations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iteration) required before the value of      z  n     {\displaystyle z_{n}}   escapes a bounded region, after which it will diverge toward [infinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinity).

It can also be described using the *[logistic map form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_quadratic_polynomial#Forms)* of the [complex quadratic map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_quadratic_map), specifically

      z  n + 1   =   M    z  n   := γ  z  n    (  1 −  z  n    )  .   {\displaystyle z_{n+1}={\mathcal {M}}z_{n}:=\gamma z_{n}\left(1-z_{n}\right).}

which is equivalent to

w  n + 1   =  w  n   2   + c   {\displaystyle w_{n+1}=w_{n}^{2}+c}  .

Irrespective of the specific iteration used, the [filled Julia set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filled_Julia_set) associated with a given value of     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   (or     μ   {\displaystyle \mu }  ) consists of all starting points      z  0     {\displaystyle z_{0}}   (or      w  0     {\displaystyle w_{0}}  ) for which the iteration remains bounded. Then, the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set) consists of those values of     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   (or     μ   {\displaystyle \mu }  ) for which the associated filled Julia set is connected. The Mandelbrot set can be viewed with respect to either     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   or     μ   {\displaystyle \mu }  .

 [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/MandelbrotLambda.jpg/500px-MandelbrotLambda.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MandelbrotLambda.jpg)The Mandelbrot set in the     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   plane[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/MandelbrotMuDouadyRabbit.jpg/250px-MandelbrotMuDouadyRabbit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MandelbrotMuDouadyRabbit.jpg)The Mandelbrot set in the     μ   {\displaystyle \mu }   plane

Noting that     μ   {\displaystyle \mu }   is invariant under the substitution     γ → 2 − γ   {\displaystyle \gamma \to 2-\gamma }  , the Mandelbrot set with respect to     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   has additional horizontal symmetry. Since     z   {\displaystyle z}   and     w   {\displaystyle w}   are [affine transformations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affine_transformation) of one another, or more specifically a similarity transformation, consisting of only scaling, rotation and translation, the filled Julia sets look [similar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Similarity_(geometry)) for either form of the iteration given above.

Detailed description

# Detailed description

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=2)] [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/DouadyRabbitInExponentialFamily.jpg/250px-DouadyRabbitInExponentialFamily.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DouadyRabbitInExponentialFamily.jpg)Douady rabbit in an exponential family [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Rabbit-lamination.png/250px-Rabbit-lamination.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rabbit-lamination.png)[Lamination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamination_(topology)) of the rabbit Julia set [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Douday_rabbit_rough_dynamics.png/250px-Douday_rabbit_rough_dynamics.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Douday_rabbit_rough_dynamics.png)Representation of the dynamics inside the rabbit

You can also describe the Douady rabbit utilising the Mandelbrot set with respect to     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   as shown in the graph above. In this figure, the Mandelbrot set superficially appears as two back-to-back [unit disks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_disk) with *sprouts* or *buds*, such as the sprouts at the one- and five-o'clock positions on the right disk or the sprouts at the seven- and eleven-o'clock positions on the left disk. When     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }   is within one of these four sprouts, the associated filled Julia set in the mapping plane is said to be a Douady rabbit. For these values of     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }  , it can be shown that       M     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}}   has     z = 0   {\displaystyle z=0}   and one other point as unstable (repelling) fixed points, and     z = ∞   {\displaystyle z=\infty }   as an attracting fixed point. Moreover, the map        M    3     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}^{3}}   has three attracting fixed points. A Douady rabbit consists of the three attracting fixed points      z  1     {\displaystyle z_{1}}  ,      z  2     {\displaystyle z_{2}}  , and      z  3     {\displaystyle z_{3}}   and their basins of attraction.

For example, Figure 4 shows the Douady rabbit in the     z   {\displaystyle z}   plane when     γ =  γ  D   = 2.55268 − 0.959456 i   {\displaystyle \gamma =\gamma _{D}=2.55268-0.959456i}  , a point in the five-o'clock sprout of the right disk. For this value of     γ   {\displaystyle \gamma }  , the map       M     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}}   has the repelling fixed points     z = 0   {\displaystyle z=0}   and     z = .656747 − .129015 i   {\displaystyle z=.656747-.129015i}  . The three attracting fixed points of        M    3     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}^{3}}   (also called period-three fixed points) have the locations

          z  1      = 0.499997032420304 − ( 1.221880225696050 ×  10  − 6   ) i         ( r e d )   ,      z  2      = 0.638169999974373 − ( 0.239864000011495 ) i         ( g r e e n )   ,      z  3      = 0.799901291393262 − ( 0.107547238170383 ) i         ( y e l l o w )   .       {\displaystyle {\begin{aligned}z_{1}&=0.499997032420304-(1.221880225696050\times 10^{-6})i{\;}{\;}{\mathrm {(red)} },\\z_{2}&=0.638169999974373-(0.239864000011495)i{\;}{\;}{\mathrm {(green)} },\\z_{3}&=0.799901291393262-(0.107547238170383)i{\;}{\;}{\mathrm {(yellow)} }.\end{aligned}}}

The red, green, and yellow points lie in the basins     B (  z  1   )   {\displaystyle B(z_{1})}  ,     B (  z  2   )   {\displaystyle B(z_{2})}  , and     B (  z  3   )   {\displaystyle B(z_{3})}   of        M    3     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}^{3}}  , respectively. The white points lie in the basin     B ( ∞ )   {\displaystyle B(\infty )}   of       M     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}}  .

The action of       M     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}}   on these fixed points is given by the relations       M    z  1   =  z  2     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}z_{1}=z_{2}}  ,       M    z  2   =  z  3     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}z_{2}=z_{3}}  , and       M    z  3   =  z  1     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}z_{3}=z_{1}}  .

Corresponding to these relations there are the results

           M   B (  z  1   )    = B (  z  2   )      o r        M        r e d   ⊆   g r e e n   ,       M   B (  z  2   )    = B (  z  3   )      o r        M        g r e e n   ⊆   y e l l o w   ,       M   B (  z  3   )    = B (  z  1   )      o r        M        y e l l o w   ⊆   r e d   .       {\displaystyle {\begin{aligned}{\mathcal {M}}B(z_{1})&=B(z_{2}){\;}{\mathrm {or} }{\;}{\mathcal {M}}{\;}{\mathrm {red} }\subseteq {\mathrm {green} },\\{\mathcal {M}}B(z_{2})&=B(z_{3}){\;}{\mathrm {or} }{\;}{\mathcal {M}}{\;}{\mathrm {green} }\subseteq {\mathrm {yellow} },\\{\mathcal {M}}B(z_{3})&=B(z_{1}){\;}{\mathrm {or} }{\;}{\mathcal {M}}{\;}{\mathrm {yellow} }\subseteq {\mathrm {red} }.\end{aligned}}}   [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/ColorDouadyRabbit1.jpg/500px-ColorDouadyRabbit1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ColorDouadyRabbit1.jpg)Figure 4: Douady rabbit for     γ = 2.55268 − 0.959456 i   {\displaystyle \gamma =2.55268-0.959456i}   or     μ = 0.122565 − 0.744864 i   {\displaystyle \mu =0.122565-0.744864i}

As a second example, Figure 5 shows a Douady rabbit when     γ = 2 −  γ  D   = − .55268 + .959456 i   {\displaystyle \gamma =2-\gamma _{D}=-.55268+.959456i}  , a point in the eleven-o'clock sprout on the left disk (    μ   {\displaystyle \mu }   is invariant under this transformation). This rabbit is more symmetrical in the plane. The period-three fixed points then are located at

          z  1      = 0.500003730675024 + ( 6.968273875812428 ×  10  − 6   ) i       (   r e d   ) ,      z  2      = − 0.138169999969259 + ( 0.239864000061970 ) i       (   g r e e n   ) ,      z  3      = − 0.238618870661709 − ( 0.264884797354373 ) i       (   y e l l o w   ) .       {\displaystyle {\begin{aligned}z_{1}&=0.500003730675024+(6.968273875812428\times 10^{-6})i{\;}{\;}({\mathrm {red} }),\\z_{2}&=-0.138169999969259+(0.239864000061970)i{\;}{\;}({\mathrm {green} }),\\z_{3}&=-0.238618870661709-(0.264884797354373)i{\;}{\;}({\mathrm {yellow} }).\end{aligned}}}

The repelling fixed points of       M     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}}   itself are located at     z = 0   {\displaystyle z=0}   and     z = 1.450795 + 0.7825835 i   {\displaystyle z=1.450795+0.7825835i}  . The three major lobes on the left, which contain the period-three fixed points      z  1     {\displaystyle z_{1}}  ,     z  2     {\displaystyle z_{2}}  , and      z  3     {\displaystyle z_{3}}  , meet at the fixed point     z = 0   {\displaystyle z=0}  , and their counterparts on the right meet at the point     z = 1   {\displaystyle z=1}  . It can be shown that the effect of       M     {\displaystyle {\mathcal {M}}}   on points near the origin consists of a counterclockwise rotation about the origin of     arg ⁡ ( γ )   {\displaystyle \arg(\gamma )}  , or very nearly      120  ∘     {\displaystyle 120^{\circ }}  , followed by scaling (dilation) by a factor of      |  γ  |  = 1.1072538   {\displaystyle |\gamma |=1.1072538}  .

 [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/ColorDouadyRabbit2.jpg/500px-ColorDouadyRabbit2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ColorDouadyRabbit2.jpg)Figure 5: Douady rabbit for     γ = − 0.55268 + 0.959456 i   {\displaystyle \gamma =-0.55268+0.959456i}   or     μ = 0.122565 − 0.744864 i   {\displaystyle \mu =0.122565-0.744864i}

Variants

# Variants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=3)]

A *twisted rabbit*[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-1) is the composition of a rabbit [polynomial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynomial) with     n   {\displaystyle n}   powers of [Dehn twists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehn_twist) about its ears.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-2)

The *corabbit* is the symmetrical image of the rabbit. Here parameter     c ≈ − 0.1226 − 0.7449 i   {\displaystyle c\approx -0.1226-0.7449i}  . It is one of 2 other [polynomials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynomial) inducing the same [permutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permutation) of their post-critical set are the rabbit.

3D

# 3D

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=4)]

The Julia set has no direct analog in three dimensions.

4D

# 4D

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=5)]

A [quaternion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternion) Julia set with parameters     c = − 0.123 + 0.745 i   {\displaystyle c=-0.123+0.745i}   and a [cross-section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_section_(geometry)) in the     x y   {\displaystyle xy}   plane. The Douady rabbit is visible in the cross-section.

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Quaternion_Julia_Douady_rabbit.jpg/500px-Quaternion_Julia_Douady_rabbit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Quaternion_Julia_Douady_rabbit.jpg)

Embedded

# Embedded

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=6)]

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Parabolic_julia_set_c_%3D_-1.125_%2B_0.21650635094611%2Ai.png/500px-Parabolic_julia_set_c_%3D_-1.125_%2B_0.21650635094611%2Ai.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Parabolic_julia_set_c_=_-1.125_+_0.21650635094611*i.png)

A small embedded [homeomorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeomorphic) copy of rabbit in the center of a Julia set[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-3)

Fat

# Fat

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=7)]

The *fat rabbit* or *chubby rabbit* has c at the root of the 1/3-[limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set#Geometry) of the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set). It has a [parabolic fixed point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodic_points_of_complex_quadratic_mappings) with 3 [petals](https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Fractals/Iterations%20in%20the%20complex%20plane/parabolic).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-4)

n-th eared

# n-th eared

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=8)]

In general, the rabbit for the     p e r i o d − ( n + 1 )   {\displaystyle period-(n+1)}  th bulb of the main cardioid will have     n   {\displaystyle n}   ears[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-5) For example, a period four bulb rabbit has three ears.

Twisted rabbit problem

# Twisted rabbit problem

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Douady_rabbit&action=edit&section=10)]

In the early 1980s, Hubbard posed the so-called twisted rabbit problem, a polynomial classification problem. The goal is to determine Thurston equivalence types[*[definition needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please_clarify)*] of functions of [complex numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_number) that usually are not given by a formula (these are called topological polynomials):[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-7)

- given a [topological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topology) quadratic whose branch point is periodic with period three, determining which quadratic polynomial it is Thurston equivalent to
- determining the [equivalence class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equivalence_class) of twisted rabbits, i.e. composite of the rabbit polynomial with nth powers of Dehn twists about its ears.

The problem was originally solved by [Laurent Bartholdi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurent_Bartholdi) and Volodymyr Nekrashevych[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-8) using iterated [monodromic groups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monodromic_group). The generalization of the problem to the case where the number of post-critical points is arbitrarily large has been solved as well.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douady_rabbit#cite_note-9)
